stem: A prescriber's office telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy with a new prescription while the pharmacist on duty is counselling another patient. Which statements about who may take the call are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Only the pharmacist may take a new prescription by telephone.
Any pharmacy employee may take it and pass it to the pharmacist to check.
A pharmacy intern may receive a new prescription over the telephone.
An uncertified technician may take it provided the pharmacist verifies it afterwards.
A certified technician with the on-duty pharmacist's approval may receive it.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(8) provides that a pharmacy intern, or a CERTIFIED pharmacy technician WHO HAS THE APPROVAL OF THE PHARMACIST ON DUTY, may receive new prescriptions over the telephone from a prescriber or authorized agent. The technician limb carries two conditions and neither is satisfied by later verification.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation extends the function beyond the pharmacist.
choice_analysis.B: It reaches interns and certified technicians, not any employee.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: interns are named without further condition here.
choice_analysis.D: Certification is required, and later verification does not supply it.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: certification plus the on-duty pharmacist's approval.

related_facts: The caller may be the prescriber or an authorized agent
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates split between assuming only pharmacists may take the call and assuming any technician may.

reasoning_steps: Apply the two conditions attached to the technician limb
Reject after-the-fact verification as a cure
